chapters.1: Paul explains he left Titus in Crete to organize the church and appoint elders who are blameless, self-controlled, and able to teach sound doctrine. He warns about rebellious teachers, especially among the Cretans, who must be firmly corrected because they are leading people astray with false teaching for personal profit while claiming to know God but denying him by how they live.
chapters.2: Paul gives Titus specific instructions for teaching different groups in the church well: older men and women, younger women, younger men, and even servants, so that their lives match sound doctrine and make the gospel attractive to outsiders. He grounds this in the truth that God's grace has appeared to bring salvation to everyone, teaching believers to live self-controlled, godly lives while they wait for Christ's return.
chapters.3: Paul tells Titus to remind believers to be respectful and gentle toward everyone, including those in authority, remembering that they themselves were once foolish and disobedient before being saved purely by God's mercy, not their own good works. He instructs Titus to avoid pointless arguments and to firmly deal with those who cause division, closing with travel plans and a final word about devoting themselves to good works.
